Each Publication 926 and Publication 15 extract has a text derivative of its last kept page, the page that states the threshold: `pdftotext -layout` for the Publication 926 Table 1 and the 1999-2007 Special Rules table, and `pdftotext -raw` for the 2017-2025 What's New paragraph. The registry quotes each edition's threshold from its derivative.

Review round 3's note 1 found that 27 of these extracts, and the Publication 51 (2023) extract in the table's last row, carry one 873,242-byte cover JPEG. All 28 now drop the cover, because a kept page's own text states the edition: its footer reads "Publication 926 (2008)" ("Publication 926 (March 2012)" for 2012), "Publication 15 (2017)" or "Publication 51 (2023)", and the row's `cover_dropped` record names the text derivative that quotes it. Each new extract was made with `qpdf --deterministic-id --empty --pages <extract> <pages> -- <out>` from the extract at `fc1d7e04`; it has the same bytes as the same pages taken from the original, and the row's `chain` records both steps. For every kept page, pdftotext gives the same text in default, `-layout` and `-raw` modes as for that page of the extract it came from and of the original. Each text derivative keeps its bytes; its page range shifts down by one. On the 2017-2020 and 2022-2025 Publication 15 editions the dropped cover page also holds What's New's heading and opening paragraphs; no citation quotes them, and the cited election-workers paragraph and the edition footer sit on the kept page 2. The other 17 extracts keep their first page, and none carries the shared cover JPEG: the seven Statutes at Large and Federal Register extracts begin with the act's or issue's own first page, each 1999-2007 Publication 15 extract is 24-188 KB in all, and the 1985 Form 1040 instructions are a scan with no text layer. The 28 extracts total 2,919,037 bytes, down from 32,845,153. The Publication 51 (2023) extract's derivative is `pdftotext -f 1 -l 3 -raw` of all three kept pages, which keeps each column's sentences contiguous across the two-column pages.
